transition_invariants: Evidence is append-only: each bit records that a qualifying observation has occurred and never flips from true to false.
FAIL is absorbing because d remains true under every evidence extension.
Before authoritative finality, b+r plus any nonfinal singleton is still UNRESOLVED; there is no actual PASS output before f+s.
A pre-final PASS candidate is therefore only diagnostic shorthand for b+r with no d; authoritative duplicate evidence before finality maps that UNRESOLVED candidate directly to FAIL.
After PASS, any later authoritative duplicate sets d=true and must transition PASS to FAIL; it cannot be ignored. Such a trace also falsifies or narrows the earlier claimed finality scope.
Non-authoritative acknowledgements, timeouts, repository ownership state, response aliases, and pre-final singleton snapshots never set f, s, or d by themselves.

bounded_leaf_result.proof_sketch: Because evidence bits are append-only, d once observed is permanent and FAIL has precedence, so FAIL is absorbing. PASS can first occur only when b,r,f,s are all true and d is false. Any extension that does not add d leaves those witnesses true and preserves PASS. Any extension that adds d moves PASS to FAIL, which is upward in the declared conservative-information order. Before finality, even b+r is UNRESOLVED, so a late duplicate does not demote an actual PASS; it converts an unresolved pass-candidate to FAIL. After finality, a later authoritative duplicate cannot be ignored: d precedence forces FAIL and simultaneously shows that the earlier finality claim was not valid for the broadened temporal scope.
